subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model `input` audio/video values be valid metadata, rejected unsupported runtime capabilities, or allowed only behind an explicit capability-override contract?
rationale: Current main has conflicting signals across schema, types, docs, tests, and runtime selection; changing only one layer could either break existing configs or keep accepting misleading capabilities.

options.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid catalog metadata, but add semantic runtime/load-time validation and diagnostics when a selected path cannot actually satisfy the declared capability.

options.title: Tighten to text/image
options.body: Reject audio/video in configured model inputs and add a doctor migration or compatibility note for configs created under the current wider contract.

options.title: Require explicit override
options.body: Allow operators to assert unsupported or unverified capabilities only through a named opt-in contract with docs and tests for the failure mode.

recommendation.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
recommendation.body: Keep audio/video as valid catalog metadata, but add semantic runtime/load-time validation and diagnostics when a selected path cannot actually satisfy the declared capability.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent provider/model architecture history makes this the best available routing owner for the cross-surface contract decision.
